Increased Use of Aluminum and Plastics
,
1
Ford Motor Company. Ford stated that the 18.7 mpg proposed requirement for NPA's for MY 1979 should be reduced to 16.3 mpg because of the fuel economy penalty of the MY 1979 emission standard and test procedure changes. They state that if this does not occur all environmental impacts will increase, especially resulting from the increased substitution of aluminum and plastics for cast iron and steel, and costs will increase.
Analysis. The final rule is based on a scenario that does not project further substitutions of aluminum and plastic for cast iron and steel. Costs therefore are also not affected.
Materials Usage Implications of the Draft EIS
Ford Motor Company. Ford stated that the draft EIS relates fuel economy improvement to vehicle weight reduction primarily due to engine CID reduction. They state that for future years, a higher fuel economy requirement would force further vehicle weight reduction through light metals and plastics substitutions. Thus, they state that environmental and energy impacts would be greater.
